histogram.name: Aerie.Adblock.CosmeticRuleCount
histogram.summary: How many hide rules the Filter Engine put in one cosmetic stylesheet, one sample for each stylesheet it built for a page (when the page committed, and when it had loaded). Zero when no rule applied. Nothing is recorded when cosmetic filtering is off for the site. The Bench uses it to show that the engine, and not other CSS, hid the ad containers.

histogram.name: Aerie.Adblock.EngineLoadSuccess
histogram.summary: Whether the Filter Engine loaded the filter engine that ships in the build. Recorded once at startup. False crashes the browser right after, because the engine is part of the build and a failure to load it means the build is broken. The Bench requires a true sample.

histogram.name: Aerie.Adblock.EngineLoadTime
histogram.summary: How long the Filter Engine took to load the serialized engine (EasyList and EasyPrivacy) at startup, on its own sequence. Requests wait for it.

histogram.name: Aerie.Adblock.RedirectHopBlocked
histogram.summary: One sample for each redirect hop of a judged request that the Filter Engine judged: true if it blocked the hop, false if it let it through. Also counted in Aerie.Adblock.RequestBlocked. The Bench uses it to show that the engine, not another blocker, stopped a redirect.

histogram.name: Aerie.Adblock.RequestBlocked
histogram.summary: One sample for each request the Filter Engine judged: true if it blocked the request, false if it let it through. Requests that never reach the engine (other schemes, main frame documents, requests another blocker already stopped) have no sample. The Bench uses it to tell the engine's blocking from another blocker's.
